chunks: And the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said: “When I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by the location of Masjid al-Kūfah while I was on al-Burāq, and Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام was with me. So he said to me: ‘O Muḥammad, descend and perform salat (prayer) in this place.’
He said: So I descended and performed salat (prayer), then I said: ‘O Jibrāʾīl, what place is this?’
He said: ‘O Muḥammad, this is Kūfān, and this is its mosque. As for me, I have indeed seen it twenty times in ruin and twenty times in prosperity, with five hundred years between every two times.’”

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ: was taken on the Night Journey
key_terms.اَلْبُرَاقِ: al-Burāq; the mount used during the heavenly journey
key_terms.اَلْكُوفَةِ: Kūfah; the city whose mosque is mentioned
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl; the angel accompanying the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.خَمْسُمِائَةِ سَنَةٍ: five hundred years; the interval between the states mentioned
key_terms.عُمْرَانًا: in a state of prosperity and habitation
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ: mosque; the sacred place of worship being referred to

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the virtue and history of Masjid al-Kūfah during the Prophet’s Night Journey?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that during the Isra', the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was instructed by Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام to descend and perform salat (prayer) at the site of Masjid al-Kūfah. It highlights the sanctity and ancient significance of the mosque, describing its repeated cycles of ruin and restoration across long spans of time.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.695 - The Prophet, said:
"When I was taken on the Night Journey (Isra'), I passed by the site of the Mosque of Kufa while I was on al-Buraq, with Archangel Jibril (as) accompanying me.
Archangel Jibril (as) said to me, 'O’ Muhammad, descend and pray at this place.'
So, I descended and prayed.
Then I asked: 'O’ Archangel Jibril (as), what is this place?'
Archangel Jibril (as) said: 'O’ Muhammad, this is Kufa, and this is its mosque. As for me, I have seen it twenty times in a state of ruin and twenty times in a state of prosperity, with five hundred years between each state.'"
